_README: Memory bandwidth per GPU, in GB/s (10^9 bytes/s), keyed by the name
tensor-override.py uses these numbers to pick the -ts for -sm tensor.
Tensor parallelism makes both cards work CONCURRENTLY, so a token costs
max_i(bytes_i / BW_i) instead of the sum, and that max is minimised when
every card finishes at the same time:   ts_i = BW_i / sum(BW).
Nothing else in the script needs these, so an entry that is merely close
is fine -- only the RATIO between your cards moves the chosen -ts.
Add your own cards below. Lookup is exact name first, then
overrides everything without editing this file.
_cpu_gb_s is system RAM bandwidth. It is used only to price blocks that
have to spill out of VRAM into RAM (-ngl below the block count), so it
only has to be the right order of magnitude. Rough guide: dual-channel
